# XboxDecomp snapshot

`xboxdecomp/` is the user-provided XboxDecomp/Xbox-XBERecomp SDK, copied as source with its MIT license and third-party notices. The source directories supplied by the user are unchanged.

`xboxdecomp.provenance.json` records the original 95-file snapshot and its SHA-256 fingerprints. No upstream Git revision was available in the supplied directory, so this is a content-pinned snapshot, not a claimed checkout of a particular commit.

`xboxdecomp.local-changes.json` records maintained patches and added files, including original/patched digests and reviewable diffs under `patches/`. The scanner patch adds explicit `--signature-build` research scans and machine-readable evidence. It does not declare XDK 5455 compatible with another build. Default scanning behavior remains unchanged.

The mixer patch implements `IDirectSoundBuffer_SetNotificationPositions`: it copies byte-offset/event pairs into host-owned voice state and signals guest events as playback crosses those positions or stops. Its cursor traversal helper has standalone native tests for boundary crossings, looping, stop markers and ADPCM positions. The imported game independently establishes the API address and three-argument contract. Event semantics follow Microsoft's [notification documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/ee418245(v=vs.85)). Registration currently limits arrays to 4096 entries.

Pinned dependency sources are fetched into ignored `local/native-deps`; their individual provenance is recorded beside the source. Game code generated by the SDK is private output under ignored `native/generated`. No Darkwatch game integration or game content is vendored.

The volume-geometry patch replaces hardcoded 16/8 GiB total/free figures with host-bounded allocation counts capped below 4 GiB. Heroes truncates XAPI byte counts to 32 bits before counting save blocks, so the previous figures became zero. The portable helper tests cover overflow, rounding and full disks; volume queries also validate handles and buffer lengths. This is a compatibility geometry report, not a claim that a separately allocated FATX disk image exists.

The controller-discovery patch defers the first port scan to the existing poller. Heroes constructs its input object after `XInitDevices`; immediate discovery let a construction-time `XGetDevices` consume the initial insertion before that object could handle it. The diagnostic logging patch enables Info/Debug release messages only when `XBE_VERBOSE` is set.

The render-capture patch adds raw texture-byte dumps, native float position/UV inputs, fixed-function matrices and texture sampling state to opt-in F3 captures. Capture-enabled launches also log skipped inline texture-offset/format commands. Its current-color correction also preserves vertex attribute 3 across draws without a diffuse input array; the old fallback to white made the damage glyph and its offset shadow appear as two white copies. Native tests exercise fixed-function and programmable shader generation, while private-image checks establish the title setter. The capture diagnostics themselves do not change normal rendering. Captures and source bytes stay in ignored private directories. A trial wrap-to-clamp restriction did not improve the reported seams and was reverted.

The frame-pacing change shares a phase-aligned 60 Hz clock between the vertical-blank interrupt and explicit waits. Explicit waits consume the remaining interval instead of adding a full 16 ms after rendering work. Its new clock helper has native tests for work within a frame, missed ticks and long sequences. Opt-in performance logs distinguish vertical-blank and frame-cap waits. Changes to the already patched D3D8/D3D12 files are included in the maintained render-capture diff; the additional host files and clock header are in `patches/xboxdecomp-frame-pacing.patch`.

The Heroes integration hooks its reviewed screen-copy path before the surface locks. For separate LIN_A8R8G8B8 surfaces, the original branch only calls CopyRects and releases both surfaces: the host issues the same copy without the unused CPU locks, retaining GPU ownership. Other formats retain their original locking and CPU conversion. `HEROES_CPU_SCREEN_COPY=1` restores the original path for comparisons. The hook and release tail are checked against the fingerprinted private executable.
